/// Emit an event. Non-blocking — returns immediately.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Err` only if the channel is disconnected (background task died).\n    pub fn emit(&self, kind: EventKind) -> Result<()> {\n        let seq = self.sequence.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);\n        let (trace_id, span_id) = current_trace_ids();\n        let event = TelemetryEvent {\n            timestamp: Utc::now(),\n            event_type: kind.event_type().to_string(),\n            worker_id: self.worker_id.clone(),\n            session_id: self.session_id.clone(),\n            sequence: seq,\n            bead_id: kind.bead_id(),\n            workspace: None,\n            duration_ms: kind.duration_ms(),\n            data: kind.to_data(),\n            trace_id,\n            span_id,\n        };\n        tracing::debug!(event_type = %event.event_type, seq, \"telemetry event\");\n        // Use try_lock() to avoid blocking indefinitely if the telemetry writer\n        // is stuck holding the lock. If the lock is contended, we log and return\n        // Ok(()) to allow the worker to continue.\n        match self.sender.try_lock() {\n            Ok(guard) => {\n                if let Some(ref s) = *guard {\n                    s.send(WriterMessage::Event(event)).ok(); // ok() — never block, never panic\n                }\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    event_type = %event.event_type,\n                    seq,\n                    \"telemetry sender lock contended, skipping emit\"\n                );\n                Ok(())\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Emit an event without blocking — uses try_lock() instead of lock().\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Ok(())` if emitted successfully or if the lock is contended\n    /// (gracefully degrades). Returns `Err` only if the channel is disconnected.\n    ///\n    /// Use this in timeout recovery paths where blocking on emit() would\n    /// prevent the worker from recovering.\n    pub fn emit_try_lock(&self, kind: EventKind) -> Result<()> {\n        let seq = self.sequence.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);\n        let (trace_id, span_id) = current_trace_ids();\n        let event = TelemetryEvent {\n            timestamp: Utc::now(),\n            event_type: kind.event_type().to_string(),\n            worker_id: self.worker_id.clone(),\n            session_id: self.session_id.clone(),\n            sequence: seq,\n            bead_id: kind.bead_id(),\n            workspace: None,\n            duration_ms: kind.duration_ms(),\n            data: kind.to_data(),\n            trace_id,\n            span_id,\n        };\n        // Use try_lock() to avoid blocking indefinitely if the telemetry writer\n        // is stuck holding the lock. If the lock is contended, we log and return\n        // Ok(()) to allow the worker to continue.\n        match self.sender.try_lock() {\n            Ok(guard) => {\n                if let Some(ref s) = *guard {\n                    s.send(WriterMessage::Event(event)).ok();\n                }\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    event_type = %event.event_type,\n                    seq,\n                    \"telemetry sender lock contended, skipping emit in timeout recovery path\"\n                );\n                Ok(())\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Force-flush all buffered events to disk (synchronous).\n    ///\n    /// Sends a flush request through the writer channel and waits (up to\n    /// `timeout`) for the writer task to flush its BufWriter. Used after\n    /// `worker.booting` so the event is visible on disk even if subsequent\n    /// init steps block.\n    ///\n    /// NOTE: This uses `blocking_recv()` and must be called from outside a\n    /// tokio runtime (e.g., in `run_worker` before `rt.block_on`). Use\n    /// `force_flush_async()` from within async contexts.\n    pub fn force_flush(&self, timeout: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {\n        let (tx, rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel();\n        // Use try_lock() to avoid blocking indefinitely if the telemetry writer\n        // is stuck holding the lock.\n        match self.sender.try_lock() {\n            Ok(guard) => {\n                if let Some(ref s) = *guard {\n                    s.send(WriterMessage::Flush(tx)).ok();\n                }\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\"telemetry sender lock contended in force_flush, skipping flush\");\n                return Ok(()); // Don't fail — the writer will eventually flush\n            }\n        }\n        // Block until the writer task flushes or timeout.\n        // Spawn a thread to handle the blocking recv with a timeout.\n        let handle = std::thread::spawn(move || rx.blocking_recv());\n        let start = std::time::Instant::now();\n        loop {\n            if handle.is_finished() {\n                return Ok(());\n            }\n            if start.elapsed() >= timeout {\n                tracing::warn!(\"force_flush timed out after {:?}\", timeout);\n                return Ok(()); // Don't fail — the writer will eventually flush\n            }\n            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(50));\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Force-flush all buffered events to disk (async).\n    ///\n    /// Async version of `force_flush()` that can be called from within a\n    /// tokio runtime. Use this in `Worker::run()` and other async contexts.\n    pub async fn force_flush_async(&self, timeout: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {\n        let (tx, rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel();\n        // Use try_lock() to avoid blocking indefinitely if the telemetry writer\n        // is stuck holding the lock.\n        match self.sender.try_lock() {\n            Ok(guard) => {\n                if let Some(ref s) = *guard {\n                    s.send(WriterMessage::Flush(tx)).ok();\n                }\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    \"telemetry sender lock contended in force_flush_async, skipping flush\"\n                );\n                return Ok(()); // Don't fail — the writer will eventually flush\n            }\n        }\n        // Wait for the writer task to flush, with timeout.\n        match tokio::time::timeout(timeout, rx).await {\n            Ok(Ok(())) => Ok(()),\n            Ok(Err(_)) => Ok(()), // Channel closed, writer already flushed\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\"force_flush_async timed out after {:?}\", timeout);\n                Ok(())\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Emit an event synchronously, writing directly to the file sink.\n    ///\n    /// This bypasses the async channel and writes immediately to the file.\n    /// Use this for critical early-boot events (like `worker.booting`) that\n    /// must be visible even if the async writer hasn't started yet.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Err` if the pending writer is not available (already started)\n    /// or if writing to the file fails.\n    pub fn emit_sync(&self, kind: EventKind) -> Result<()> {\n        let seq = self.sequence.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);\n        let (trace_id, span_id) = current_trace_ids();\n        let event = TelemetryEvent {\n            timestamp: Utc::now(),\n            event_type: kind.event_type().to_string(),\n            worker_id: self.worker_id.clone(),\n            session_id: self.session_id.clone(),\n            sequence: seq,\n            bead_id: kind.bead_id(),\n            workspace: None,\n            duration_ms: kind.duration_ms(),\n            data: kind.to_data(),\n            trace_id,\n            span_id,\n        };\n\n        // Take the pending writer temporarily to write directly to sinks.\n        let pending_guard = self.pending_writer.lock().unwrap();\n        if let Some(ref pending) = *pending_guard {\n            // Write directly to each sink (typically just FileSink).\n            for sink in &pending.sinks {\n                if let Err(e) = sink.accept(&event) {\n                    tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"sync emit to sink failed\");\n                }\n            }\n            Ok(())\n        } else {\n            // Pending writer already consumed by start().\n            Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"cannot emit_sync after start()\"))\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Return a reference to the session ID for log path discovery.\n    pub fn session_id(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.session_id\n    }\n\n    /// Return a reference to the worker ID.\n    pub fn worker_id(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.worker_id\n    }\n\n    /// Create a telemetry emitter writing to a specific log directory.\n    ///\n    /// Use this when the config specifies a custom log path. Does not spawn\n    /// any async tasks. Call [`start()`](Self::start) from within a tokio\n    /// runtime context before emitting events.\n    pub fn with_log_dir(worker_id: WorkerId, log_dir: &Path) -> Self {\n        let session_id = generate_session_id();\n        let (sender, receiver) = mpsc::unbounded_channel();\n\n        let mut sinks: Vec<Box<dyn Sink>> = Vec::new();\n        match FileSink::with_dir(log_dir, &worker_id, &session_id) {\n            Ok(s) => sinks.push(Box::new(s)),\n            Err(e) => tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"failed to create telemetry file sink\"),\n        }\n\n        let sequence = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));\n        let pending = PendingWriter { receiver, sinks };\n\n        Telemetry {\n            worker_id,\n            session_id,\n            sequence,\n            sender: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(sender))),\n            pending_writer: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(pending))),\n            writer_handle: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),\n            otlp_shutdown: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Start the background writer task.\n    ///\n    /// Must be called from within a tokio runtime context (e.g. inside\n    /// `block_on` or an async function). Calling this more than once on\n    /// the same handle is a no-op.\n    pub fn start(&self) {\n        let pending = self.pending_writer.lock().unwrap().take();\n        if let Some(pw) = pending {\n            let handle = Self::spawn_writer(pw.receiver, pw.sinks, None);\n            *self.writer_handle.lock().unwrap() = Some(handle);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Start the background writer task and wait for it to be ready.\n    ///\n    /// Returns a Future that completes when the writer thread has started\n    /// and is ready to process events. Use this instead of `start()` when\n    /// you need to guarantee that events emitted immediately after will\n    /// be processed (e.g., for `worker.booting` as the first JSONL event).\n    ///\n    /// Must be called from within a tokio runtime context.\n    pub async fn start_and_wait(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        eprintln!(\"NEEDLE telemetry: starting writer thread and waiting for ready signal...\");\n        let pending = self.pending_writer.lock().unwrap().take();\n        if let Some(pw) = pending {\n            let (ready_tx, ready_rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel();\n            let handle = Self::spawn_writer(pw.receiver, pw.sinks, Some(ready_tx));\n            *self.writer_handle.lock().unwrap() = Some(handle);\n\n            // Wait for the writer thread to signal it's ready.\n            // Use a timeout to avoid hanging if the thread fails to start.\n            eprintln!(\"NEEDLE telemetry: waiting for writer thread ready signal (timeout 5s)...\");\n            tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5), ready_rx)\n                .await\n                .map_err(|_| anyhow::anyhow!(\"writer thread failed to start within 5s\"))?\n                .map_err(|_| anyhow::anyhow!(\"writer thread closed before signaling ready\"))?;\n            eprintln!(\"NEEDLE telemetry: writer thread ready signal received\");\n        } else {\n            eprintln!(\"NEEDLE telemetry: writer thread already started, skipping\");\n        }\n        eprintln!(\"NEEDLE telemetry: start_and_wait complete\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Flush and shut down the background writer.\n    ///\n    /// Drops the shared sender (closing the channel) so the writer thread\n    /// processes all buffered events and flushes its `BufWriter` before\n    /// exiting. Joins the thread to guarantee completion.\n    ///\n    /// Call this at every terminal path in the worker before the tokio\n    /// Runtime is dropped, or the BufWriter flush will be cancelled.\n    pub async fn shutdown(&self) {\n        // Drop the sender to signal EOF to the writer thread.\n        *self.sender.lock().unwrap() = None;\n        // Join the writer thread so the flush completes before we return.\n        let handle = self.writer_handle.lock().unwrap().take();\n        if let Some(h) = handle {\n            let _ = h.join();\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Shut down the OTLP sink gracefully (if enabled).\n    ///\n    /// This drains all batched OTLP exports before returning. Should be called\n    /// once at process exit, before the Tokio runtime is dropped.\n    ///\n    /// This is a no-op if the OTLP sink is not configured or if the `otlp`\n    /// feature is disabled.\n    pub async fn shutdown_otlp(&self) {\n        let shutdown = self.otlp_shutdown.lock().unwrap().take();\n        if let Some(s) = shutdown {\n            if let Err(e) = s.shutdown().await {\n                tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"OTLP shutdown failed\");\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Record the current queue depth for the `needle.queue.depth` observable gauge.\n    ///\n    /// This updates the per-priority counts that the observable gauge callback reads.\n    /// The queue depth should be sampled during strand evaluation (typically after\n    /// the Pluck strand returns candidates).\n    ///\n    /// The `depths` parameter maps priority level -> bead count at that priority.\n    ///\n    /// This is a no-op if the OTLP sink is not configured or if the `otlp`\n    /// feature is disabled.\n    pub fn record_queue_depth(&self, depths: std::collections::HashMap<u8, u64>) {\n        #[cfg(feature = \"otlp\")]\n        {\n            let shutdown = self.otlp_shutdown.lock().unwrap();\n            if let Some(OtlpShutdown::Sink(sink)) = &*shutdown {\n                sink.record_queue_depth(depths);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Spawn background writer task draining the channel to all registered sinks.\n    ///\n    /// Spawns a dedicated thread with its own tokio runtime so the writer task\n    /// can immediately start processing messages, even before the main runtime's\n    /// `block_on()` is called. This fixes a deadlock where `force_flush()` would\n    /// wait indefinitely for a response from a task that hasn't started yet.\n    ///\n    /// If `ready_signal` is provided, sends () through it when the writer is\n    /// ready to process events.\n    fn spawn_writer(\n        receiver: mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<WriterMessage>,\n        sinks: Vec<Box<dyn Sink>>,\n        ready_signal: Option<tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<()>>,\n    ) -> std::thread::JoinHandle<()> {\n        std::thread::spawn(move || {\n            let rt = match tokio::runtime::Runtime::new() {\n                Ok(r) => r,\n                Err(e) => {\n                    // Fallback to stderr when tracing may not be initialized yet\n                    eprintln!(\n                        \"NEEDLE telemetry writer thread: FAILED to create tokio runtime: {}\",\n                        e\n                    );\n                    tracing::error!(error = %e, \"failed to create writer runtime\");\n                    // Signal that we failed (by dropping the sender without sending)\n                    drop(ready_signal);\n                    return;\n                }\n            };\n            eprintln!(\"NEEDLE telemetry writer thread: started successfully\");\n            if sinks.is_empty() {\n                eprintln!(\"NEEDLE telemetry writer thread: WARNING - no sinks configured, events will be discarded!\");\n            }\n            let mut receiver = receiver;\n            rt.block_on(async move {\n                // Signal that the writer is ready to process events.\n                // Do this before entering the recv() loop so the caller\n                // can proceed as soon as we're ready.\n                eprintln!(\"NEEDLE telemetry writer thread: signaling ready to main thread...\");\n                if let Some(tx) = ready_signal {\n                    tx.send(()).ok();\n                }\n                eprintln!(\"NEEDLE telemetry writer thread: ready, waiting for events...\");\n\n                let deadline = std::time::Duration::from_secs(5);\n                let mut event_count = 0u64;\n                while let Some(msg) = receiver.recv().await {\n                    match msg {\n                        WriterMessage::Event(event) => {\n                            event_count += 1;\n                            for sink in &sinks {\n                                if let Err(e) = sink.accept(&event) {\n                                    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE telemetry: sink accept failed for event {}: {}\", event.event_type, e);\n                                    tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"telemetry sink accept failed\");\n                                }\n                            }\n                            if event_count == 1 {\n                                eprintln!(\"NEEDLE telemetry writer thread: first event written: {}\", event.event_type);\n                            }\n                        }\n                        WriterMessage::Flush(reply) => {\n                            for sink in &sinks {\n                                if let Err(e) = sink.flush(deadline) {\n                                    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE telemetry: sink flush failed: {}\", e);\n                                    tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"telemetry sink flush on demand failed\");\n                                }\n                            }\n                            reply.send(()).ok();\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n                for sink in &sinks {\n                    if let Err(e) = sink.flush(deadline) {\n                        tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"telemetry sink flush failed\");\n                    }\n                }\n            })\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Log querying ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Parse a `--since` value into a `DateTime<Utc>`.\n///\n/// Accepts relative durations like `1h`, `30m`, `24h`, `7d` or absolute\n/// ISO 8601 / date strings like `2026-03-20` or `2026-03-20T15:00:00Z`.\npub fn parse_since(input: &str) -> Result<DateTime<Utc>> {\n    let trimmed = input.trim();\n\n    // Try relative duration: Nh, Nm, Nd, Ns\n    if let Some(rest) = trimmed.strip_suffix('h') {\n        let hours: i64 = rest.parse().context(\"invalid hours in --since\")?;\n        return Ok(Utc::now() - chrono::Duration::hours(hours));\n    }\n    if let Some(rest) = trimmed.strip_suffix('m') {\n        let mins: i64 = rest.parse().context(\"invalid minutes in --since\")?;\n        return Ok(Utc::now() - chrono::Duration::minutes(mins));\n    }\n    if let Some(rest) = trimmed.strip_suffix('d') {\n        let days: i64 = rest.parse().context(\"invalid days in --since\")?;\n        return Ok(Utc::now() - chrono::Duration::days(days));\n    }\n    if let Some(rest) = trimmed.strip_suffix('s') {\n        if rest.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) {\n            let secs: i64 = rest.parse().context(\"invalid seconds in --since\")?;\n            return Ok(Utc::now() - chrono::Duration::seconds(secs));\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Try ISO 8601 with time\n    if let Ok(dt) = trimmed.parse::<DateTime<Utc>>() {\n        return Ok(dt);\n    }\n\n    // Try date-only (YYYY-MM-DD) → midnight UTC\n    if let Ok(date) = chrono::NaiveDate::parse_from_str(trimmed, \"%Y-%m-%d\") {\n        let dt = date.and_hms_opt(0, 0, 0).context(\"invalid date\")?;\n        return Ok(DateTime::from_naive_utc_and_offset(dt, Utc));\n    }\n\n    anyhow::bail!(\n        \"unrecognized --since format: '{}'. Use relative (1h, 30m, 7d) or ISO date (2026-03-20)\",\n        input\n    )\n}\n\n/// Convert a glob-style filter pattern to a regex.\n///\n/// Supports `*` as wildcard. E.g., `bead.claim.*` → `^bead\\.claim\\..*$`\npub fn glob_to_regex(pattern: &str) -> Result<regex::Regex> {\n    let mut re = String::from(\"^\");\n    for ch in pattern.chars() {\n        match ch {\n            '*' => re.push_str(\".*\"),\n            '.' => re.push_str(\"\\\\.\"),\n            '?' => re.push('.'),\n            c => re.push(c),\n        }\n    }\n    re.push('$');\n    regex::Regex::new(&re).context(\"invalid filter pattern\")\n}\n\n// ─── Rich filter expressions ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A single filter predicate applied to a telemetry event.\nenum FilterPredicate {\n    /// Glob pattern matched against `event_type` (backward-compatible).\n    EventTypeGlob(regex::Regex),\n    /// Exact case-sensitive match on a named field.\n    FieldEquals { field: String, value: String },\n    /// Regex match on a named field.\n    FieldRegex {\n        field: String,\n        pattern: regex::Regex,\n    },\n    /// Numeric greater-than on a named field.\n    FieldGt { field: String, threshold: f64 },\n}\n\n/// A conjunction (AND) of filter predicates for querying telemetry events.\n///\n/// Build from one or more expression strings with [`LogsFilter::parse`].\npub struct LogsFilter {\n    predicates: Vec<FilterPredicate>,\n}\n\nimpl LogsFilter {\n    /// Parse a list of filter expression strings into a `LogsFilter`.\n    ///\n    /// Each expression may be one of:\n    /// - `field=value`   — exact string match\n    /// - `field~pattern` — regex match\n    /// - `field>number`  — numeric greater-than\n    /// - `glob`          — glob pattern on `event_type` (no operator, backward compat)\n    ///\n    /// All predicates are ANDed together.\n    pub fn parse(exprs: &[&str]) -> Result<Self> {\n        let mut predicates = Vec::with_capacity(exprs.len());\n        for expr in exprs {\n            let expr = expr.trim();\n            if let Some(pos) = expr.find('=') {\n                let field = expr[..pos].to_string();\n                let value = expr[pos + 1..].to_string();\n                predicates.push(FilterPredicate::FieldEquals { field, value });\n            } else if let Some(pos) = expr.find('~') {\n                let field = expr[..pos].to_string();\n                let raw = &expr[pos + 1..];\n                let pattern = regex::Regex::new(raw)\n                    .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid regex in filter '{expr}': {raw}\"))?;\n                predicates.push(FilterPredicate::FieldRegex { field, pattern });\n            } else if let Some(pos) = expr.find('>') {\n                let field = expr[..pos].to_string();\n                let raw = &expr[pos + 1..];\n                let threshold: f64 = raw\n                    .parse()\n                    .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid number in filter '{expr}': {raw}\"))?;\n                predicates.push(FilterPredicate::FieldGt { field, threshold });\n            } else {\n                // Treat as glob pattern on event_type.\n                let re = glob_to_regex(expr)?;\n                predicates.push(FilterPredicate::EventTypeGlob(re));\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(LogsFilter { predicates })\n    }\n\n    /// Return `true` if the event satisfies all predicates.\n    pub fn matches(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> bool {\n        self.predicates.iter().all(|p| predicate_matches(p, event))\n    }\n\n    /// Return `true` if the filter has no predicates (matches everything).\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.predicates.is_empty()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Evaluate a single predicate against an event.\nfn predicate_matches(pred: &FilterPredicate, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> bool {\n    match pred {\n        FilterPredicate::EventTypeGlob(re) => re.is_match(&event.event_type),\n        FilterPredicate::FieldEquals { field, value } => {\n            get_event_field_str(event, field).as_deref() == Some(value.as_str())\n        }\n        FilterPredicate::FieldRegex { field, pattern } => get_event_field_str(event, field)\n            .map(|v| pattern.is_match(&v))\n            .unwrap_or(false),\n        FilterPredicate::FieldGt { field, threshold } => get_event_field_f64(event, field)\n            .map(|v| v > *threshold)\n            .unwrap_or(false),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Extract a named field from a `TelemetryEvent` as a string.\n///\n/// Supported top-level fields: `event_type`, `worker_id`, `session_id`,\n/// `bead_id`, `workspace`. Data sub-fields can be accessed directly by\n/// name (matched against `event.data[field]`).\nfn get_event_field_str(event: &TelemetryEvent, field: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    match field {\n        \"event_type\" => Some(event.event_type.clone()),\n        \"worker_id\" => Some(event.worker_id.clone()),\n        \"session_id\" => Some(event.session_id.clone()),\n        \"bead_id\" => event.bead_id.as_ref().map(|b| b.as_ref().to_string()),\n        \"workspace\" => event.workspace.as_ref().map(|p| p.display().to_string()),\n        _ => {\n            // Check data sub-fields.\n            event.data.get(field).map(|v| match v {\n                serde_json::Value::String(s) => s.clone(),\n                other => other.to_string(),\n            })\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Extract a named field from a `TelemetryEvent` as a float.\n///\n/// Supported numeric fields: `duration_ms`, `sequence`, and any numeric key\n/// in `event.data`.\nfn get_event_field_f64(event: &TelemetryEvent, field: &str) -> Option<f64> {\n    match field {\n        \"duration_ms\" => event.duration_ms.map(|d| d as f64),\n        \"sequence\" => Some(event.sequence as f64),\n        _ => event.data.get(field).and_then(|v| v.as_f64()),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Parse a time-bound string (relative or absolute) into a UTC timestamp.\n///\n/// This is an alias for [`parse_since`] and accepts the same formats.\npub fn parse_until(input: &str) -> Result<DateTime<Utc>> {\n    parse_since(input)\n}\n\n/// Read and parse JSONL log files from a directory.\n///\n/// Returns events sorted by timestamp. Optionally filters by `since`, `until`,\n/// and a [`LogsFilter`] predicate set.\npub fn read_logs(\n    log_dir: &Path,\n    since: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,\n    until: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,\n    filter: Option<&LogsFilter>,\n) -> Result<Vec<TelemetryEvent>> {\n    let mut events = Vec::new();\n\n    if !log_dir.is_dir() {\n        return Ok(events);\n    }\n\n    let entries = std::fs::read_dir(log_dir)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"cannot read log directory: {}\", log_dir.display()))?;\n\n    for entry in entries {\n        let entry = entry?;\n        let path = entry.path();\n        if path.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()) != Some(\"jsonl\") {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let contents = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"cannot read log file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        for line in contents.lines() {\n            if line.trim().is_empty() {\n                continue;\n            }\n            let event: TelemetryEvent = match serde_json::from_str(line) {\n                Ok(e) => e,\n                Err(_) => continue, // Skip malformed lines\n            };\n            if let Some(ref cutoff) = since {\n                if event.timestamp < *cutoff {\n                    continue;\n                }\n            }\n            if let Some(ref ceiling) = until {\n                if event.timestamp > *ceiling {\n                    continue;\n                }\n            }\n            if let Some(f) = filter {\n                if !f.matches(&event) {\n                    continue;\n                }\n            }\n            events.push(event);\n        }\n    }\n\n    events.sort_by_key(|a| a.timestamp);\n    Ok(events)\n}\n\n/// Compute cost summary from effort events.\npub fn compute_cost_summary(events: &[TelemetryEvent]) -> CostSummary {\n    let mut summary = CostSummary::default();\n    for event in events {\n        if event.event_type == \"effort.recorded\" {\n            summary.total_events += 1;\n            if let Some(cost) = event.data[\"estimated_cost_usd\"].as_f64() {\n                summary.total_cost_usd += cost;\n            }\n            if let Some(tokens_in) = event.data[\"tokens_in\"].as_u64() {\n                summary.total_tokens_in += tokens_in;\n            }\n            if let Some(tokens_out) = event.data[\"tokens_out\"].as_u64() {\n                summary.total_tokens_out += tokens_out;\n            }\n            if let Some(elapsed) = event.data[\"elapsed_ms\"].as_u64() {\n                summary.total_elapsed_ms += elapsed;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    summary\n}\n\n/// Aggregated cost data from effort events.\n#[derive(Debug, Default)]\npub struct CostSummary {\n    pub total_events: u64,\n    pub total_cost_usd: f64,\n    pub total_tokens_in: u64,\n    pub total_tokens_out: u64,\n    pub total_elapsed_ms: u64,\n}\n\n/// Per-worker cost breakdown from effort events.\n#[derive(Debug, Default)]\npub struct WorkerCostSummary {\n    pub worker_id: String,\n    pub total_events: u64,\n    pub total_cost_usd: f64,\n    pub total_tokens_in: u64,\n    pub total_tokens_out: u64,\n    pub total_elapsed_ms: u64,\n}\n\n/// Compute per-worker cost breakdown from effort events.\n///\n/// Returns one entry per worker that has at least one effort event, sorted\n/// by descending total cost.\npub fn compute_cost_by_worker(events: &[TelemetryEvent]) -> Vec<WorkerCostSummary> {\n    let mut map: std::collections::HashMap<String, WorkerCostSummary> =\n        std::collections::HashMap::new();\n    for event in events {\n        if event.event_type != \"effort.recorded\" {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let entry = map\n            .entry(event.worker_id.clone())\n            .or_insert_with(|| WorkerCostSummary {\n                worker_id: event.worker_id.clone(),\n                ..Default::default()\n            });\n        entry.total_events += 1;\n        if let Some(cost) = event.data[\"estimated_cost_usd\"].as_f64() {\n            entry.total_cost_usd += cost;\n        }\n        if let Some(tokens_in) = event.data[\"tokens_in\"].as_u64() {\n            entry.total_tokens_in += tokens_in;\n        }\n        if let Some(tokens_out) = event.data[\"tokens_out\"].as_u64() {\n            entry.total_tokens_out += tokens_out;\n        }\n        if let Some(elapsed) = event.data[\"elapsed_ms\"].as_u64() {\n            entry.total_elapsed_ms += elapsed;\n        }\n    }\n    let mut result: Vec<WorkerCostSummary> = map.into_values().collect();\n    result.sort_by(|a, b| {\n        b.total_cost_usd\n            .partial_cmp(&a.total_cost_usd)\n            .unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal)\n    });\n    result\n}\n\n/// Per-workspace cost breakdown from effort events.\n#[derive(Debug, Default)]\npub struct WorkspaceCostSummary {\n    pub workspace: String,\n    pub total_events: u64,\n    pub total_cost_usd: f64,\n    pub total_tokens_in: u64,\n    pub total_tokens_out: u64,\n    pub total_elapsed_ms: u64,\n}\n\n/// Compute per-workspace cost     if event.event_type != \"effort.recorded\" {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let ws_key = event\n            .workspace\n            .as_ref()\n            .map(|p|                workspace: ws_key,\n                ..Default::default()\n            });\n        entry.total_events += 1;\n        if let Some(cost) = event.data[\"estimated_cost_usd\"].as_f64() {\n            entry.total_cost_usd += cost;\n        }\n        if let Some(tokens_in) = event.data[\"tokens_in\"].as_u64() {\n            entry.total_tokens_in += tokens_in;\n        }\n        if let Some(tokens_out) = event.data[\"tokens_out\"].as_u64() {\n            entry.total_tokens_out += tokens_out;\n        }\n        if let Some(elapsed) = event.data[\"elapsed_ms\"].as_u64() {\n            entry.total_elapsed_ms += elapsed;\n        }\n    }\n    let mut result: Vec<WorkspaceCostSummary> = map.into_values().collect();\n    result.sort_by(|a, b| {\n        b.total_cost_usd\n            .partial_cmp(&a.total_cost_usd)\n            .unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal)\n    });\n    result\n}\n\n// ─── Unit tests  }\n\n    #[tokio::test]\n    async fn telemetry_start_spawns_writer_and_delivers_events() {\n        let (sink, events) = MemorySink::new();\n        let telemetry = Telemetry::with_sink(\"test-start\".to_string(), sink);\n\n        // start() must be called from inside the runtime\n        telemetry.start();\n\n        telemetry\n            .emit(EventKind::WorkerStarted {\n                worker_name: \"test-start\".to_string(),\n                version: \"0.0.0\".to_string(),\n            })\n            .unwrap();\n\n        // Give the background task a moment to drain the channel.\n        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(50)).await;\n\n        let received = events.lock().unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(received.len(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(received[0].event_type, \"worker.started\");\n    }\n\n    /// Regression test: BufWriter never flushed on short-lived sessions.\n    ///\n    /// When a worker hits EXHAUSTED quickly the total telemetry is only a few\n    /// hundred bytes — well below BufWriter's 8 KB auto-flush threshold.\n    /// `shutdown()` must drop the sender (closing the channel) and *await* the\n    /// writer task's JoinHandle so the flush runs before the tokio Runtime drops.\n    #[tokio::test]\n    async fn shutdown_flushes_bufwriter_on_short_lived_session() {\n        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(\"needle-test-shutdown-flush\");\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);\n\n        let (telemetry, path) = Telemetry::with_log_dir_and_path(\"test-worker\".to_string(), &dir)\n            .expect(\"should create\");\n\n        // start() must be called from inside the runtime.\n        telemetry.start();\n\n        // Emit a handful of small events — total << 8 KB BufWriter threshold.\n        telemetry\n            .emit(EventKind::WorkerStarted {\n                worker_name: \"test-worker\".to_string(),\n                version: \"0.1.0\".to_string(),\n            })\n            .unwrap();\n        telemetry.emit(EventKind::QueueEmpty).unwrap();\n        telemetry\n            .emit(EventKind::WorkerStopped {\n                reason: \"exhausted\".to_string(),\n                beads_processed: 0,\n                uptime_secs: 0,\n            })\n            .unwrap();\n\n        // shutdown() closes the channel, awaits the writer task, and guarantees\n        // the BufWriter is flushed before returning — no sleep required.\n        telemetry.shutdown().await;\n\n        // The file must contain the 4 events (worker.booting is written during init,\n        // plus the 3 events emitted by the test). If the BufWriter was never\n        // flushed the file would be 0 bytes and this assertion would fail.\n        let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).expect(\"log file must exist\");\n        let lines: Vec<&str> = content.lines().filter(|l| !l.is_empty()).collect();\n        assert_eq!(\n            lines.len(),\n            4,\n            \"expected 4 JSONL lines after shutdown (worker.booting + 3 emitted events)\"\n        );\n        for line in &lines {\n            let v: serde_json::Value =\n                serde_json::from_str(line).expect(\"each line must be valid JSON\");\n            assert!(\n                v.get(\"event_type\").is_some(),\n                \"event_type field must be present\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);\n    }\n\n    /// Verify that events emitted inside an OTel span carry the correct\n    /// trace_id and span_id in 32/16 lowercase-hex W3C format.\n    #[cfg(feature = \"otlp\")]\n    #[tokio::test]\n    async fn emit_inside_span_captures_trace_and_span_ids() {\n        use opentelemetry::{\n            trace::{SpanContext, SpanId, TraceContextExt, TraceFlags, remain assigned)\"\n                    );\n                } else {\n                    tracing::error!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"br release failed — worker will continue (bead may remain assigned)\"\n                    );\n                }\n                events.push(EventKind::BeadReleaseFailed {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    reason: e.to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                // Timeout after 30s.\n                tracing::error!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"br release timed out after 30s — worker will continue (bead may remain assigned)\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::BeadReleaseFailed {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    reason: \"timeout after 30s\".to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(events)\n    }\n\n    /// Handle a process output for the given bead.\n    ///\n    /// Uses `classify()` to determine the outcome, then dispatches to the\n    /// per-outcome handler. Every `Outcome` variant has an explicit arm —\n    /// no wildcards. Returns a `HandlerResult` describing what happened.\n    #[tracing::instrument(\n        name = \"bead.outcome\",\n        skip(self, store, bead, output),\n        fields(\n            needle.bead.id = %bead.id,\n            needle.outcome = tracing::field::Empty,\n            needle.outcome.action = tracing::field::Empty,\n        )\n    )]\n    pub async fn handle(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n        output: &AgentOutcome,\n        was_interrupted: bool,\n    ) -> Result<HandlerResult> {\n        let outcome = classify(output.exit_code, was_interrupted);\n\n        // Set outcome as span attribute\n        tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.outcome\", outcome.as_str());\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            bead_id = %bead.id,\n            exit_code = output.exit_code,\n            outcome = %outcome,\n            \"handling agent outcome\"\n        );\n\n        // Use emit_try_lock() to avoid blocking if telemetry writer is stuck.\n        // This prevents worker hang in HANDLING state when telemetry is wedged.\n        let _ = self.telemetry.emit_try_lock(EventKind::OutcomeClassified {\n            bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n            outcome: outcome.as_str().to_string(),\n            exit_code: output.exit_code,\n        });\n\n        let (bead_action, telemetry_events) = match outcome.clone() {\n            Outcome::Success => self.handle_success(store, bead).await?,\n            Outcome::Failure => self.handle_failure(store, bead).await?,\n            Outcome::Timeout => self.handle_timeout(store, bead).await?,\n            Outcome::AgentNotFound => self.handle_agent_not_found(store, bead).await?,\n            Outcome::Interrupted => self.handle_interrupted(store, bead).await?,\n            Outcome::Crash(code) => self.handle_crash(store, bead, code).await?,\n        };\n\n        // Emit sub-handler events (e.g. BeadCompleted, BeadOrphaned) to the\n        // telemetry sink so they appear in the JSONL log.\n        // Use emit_try_lock() to avoid blocking if telemetry writer is stuck.\n        for event in &telemetry_events {\n            let _ = self.telemetry.emit_try_lock(event.clone());\n        }\n\n        // Use emit_try_lock() to avoid blocking if telemetry writer is stuck.\n        let _ = self.telemetry.emit_try_lock(EventKind::OutcomeHandled {\n            bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n            outcome: outcome.as_str().to_string(),\n            action: bead_action.to_string(),\n        });\n\n        // Set action as span attribute\n        tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.outcome.action\", bead_action.to_string());\n\n        // Set span status: Ok for success, Error otherwise\n        if !matches!(outcome, Outcome::Success) {\n            tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_code\", 2u64);\n            tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_description\", outcome.as_str());\n        }\n\n        Ok(HandlerResult {\n            outcome,\n            bead_action,\n            telemetry_events,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Handle a process output with cancellation support.\n    ///\n    /// Checks the cancellation flag before starting the handler and returns\n    /// early if the handler has been cancelled (e.g., due to a timeout in\n    /// the worker). This prevents the handler from making further br calls\n    /// after a timeout has occurred.\n    pub async fn handle_with_cancellation(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n        output: &AgentOutcome,\n        was_interrupted: bool,\n        cancelled: Arc<AtomicBool>,\n    ) -> Result<HandlerResult> {\n        // Check if we've been cancelled before starting.\n        if cancelled.load(Ordering::Acquire) {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                \"outcome handler cancelled before starting, returning early\"\n            );\n            // Return a default HandlerResult to allow the worker to recover.\n            return Ok(HandlerResult {\n                outcome: classify(output.exit_code, was_interrupted),\n                bead_action: BeadAction::None,\n                telemetry_events: vec![],\n            });\n        }\n\n        // Wrap the handler in a timeout to prevent indefinite hangs.\n        // This is a safety net in case the internal br call timeouts don't work.\n        let bead_id = bead.id.clone();\n        let telemetry = self.telemetry.clone();\n\n        match tokio::time::timeout(\n            std::time::Duration::from_secs(50),\n            self.handle(store, bead, output, was_interrupted),\n        )\n        .await\n        {\n            Ok(Ok(result)) => Ok(result),\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                // Handler returned an error.\n                tracing::error!(\n                    bead_id = %bead_id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"outcome handler returned error\"\n                );\n                Err(e)\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                // Timeout after 50 seconds.\n                tracing::error!(\n                    bead_id = %bead_id,\n                    \"outcome handler timed out after 50s, returning early to allow worker recovery\"\n                );\n                // Emit a timeout event for observability.\n                let _ = telemetry.emit(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                    outcome: classify(output.exit_code, was_interrupted)\n                        .as_str()\n                        .to_string(),\n                    operation: \"handle\".to_string(),\n                    error: \"timeout after 50s\".to_string(),\n                });\n                // Return a default HandlerResult to allow the worker to recover.\n                // The worker's 60-second timeout wrapper will handle best-effort release.\n                Ok(HandlerResult {\n                    outcome: classify(output.exit_code, was_interrupted),\n                    bead_action: BeadAction::Released,\n                    telemetry_events: vec![EventKind::BeadReleased {\n                        bead_id,\n                        reason: \"handler_timeout\".to_string(),\n                    }],\n                })\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Success: run validation gates (if configured), then verify bead closure.\n    ///\n    /// Flow:\n    /// 1. If validation gates are configured (new or legacy format), run them.\n    /// 2. If any gate fails: reopen the bead (if agent closed it) and release it.\n    /// 3. If all gates pass (or none configured): check if agent closed the bead.\n    ///    - Closed → emit BeadCompleted.\n    ///    - Still open → emit BeadOrphaned warning.\n    ///\n    /// NEEDLE does NOT auto-close — the agent owns closure via `br close`.\n    async fn handle_success(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        tracing::info!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"agent completed successfully\");\n\n        // Try pluggable gates first, fall back to legacy verification commands.\n        let gate = if !self.config.gates.is_empty() {\n            // New pluggable gate system.\n            let gate_configs: Vec<(String, GateConfig)> = self\n                .config\n                .gates\n                .iter()\n                .enumerate()\n                .map(|(i, config)| (format!(\"gate_{}\", i), config.clone()))\n                .collect();\n            ValidationGate::new(gate_configs, bead.workspace.clone())\n        } else if !self.config.verification.is_empty() {\n            // Legacy verification command format.\n            ValidationGate::from_commands(self.config.verification.clone(), bead.workspace.clone())\n        } else {\n            None\n        };\n\n        if let Some(gate) = gate {\n            let report = gate.run(bead).await?;\n\n            if !report.all_passed {\n                return self.handle_gate_failure(store, bead, &report).await;\n            }\n\n            // All gates passed — emit telemetry.\n            let gates_run = report.results.len() as u32;\n            self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::VerificationPassed {\n                bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                gates_run,\n            })?;\n            tracing::info!(\n                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                gates_run,\n                \"all validation gates passed\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        // Reset failure count on successful gate completion.\n        // This ensures the bead starts fresh on the next cycle if re-claimed.\n        let _ = self.reset_failure_count(store, bead).await;\n\n        // Normal success flow: check if agent closed the bead.\n        let mut events = Vec::new();\n\n        // Use timeout for show() to prevent indefinite hang in HANDLING state.\n        match self.timeout_op(|| store.show(&bead.id), \"show\").await {\n            Ok(Some(current)) if current.status.is_done() => {\n                tracing::info!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"bead confirmed closed by agent\");\n                events.push(EventKind::BeadCompleted {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    duration_ms: 0,\n                });\n                // Increment success_count for any skills that matched this bead.\n                if !bead.workspace.as_os_str().is_empty() {\n                    if let Ok(lib) = crate::skill::SkillLibrary::load(&bead.workspace) {\n                        if let Err(e) = lib.increment_success_for_bead(&bead.labels, &bead.title) {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                                error = %e,\n                                \"failed to increment skill success counts\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            Ok(Some(current)) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    status = %current.status,\n                    \"agent exited successfully but bead is still open (orphaned)\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::BeadOrphaned {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                });\n            }\n            Ok(None) => {\n                // Timeout - emit telemetry and continue.\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"show() timed out, could not verify bead closure status\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"success\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"show\".to_string(),\n                    error: \"timeout after 30s\".to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"could not verify bead closure status\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"success\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"show\".to_string(),\n                    error: e.to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Flush SQLite state to JSONL so the closed/orphaned bead is captured in\n        // the git-committed backup. Non-fatal: a flush failure is logged but does\n        // not block the worker from picking up the next bead.\n        match self.timeout_op(|| store.flush(), \"flush\").await {\n            Ok(Some(())) => {\n                tracing::debug!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"flushed bead state to JSONL after success\");\n            }\n            Ok(None) => {\n                tracing::warn!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"flush timed out after success — JSONL may lag SQLite\");\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(bead_id = %bead.id, error = %e, \"flush failed after success — JSONL may lag SQLite\");\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok((BeadAction::None, events))\n    }\n\n    /// Handle gate failure: reopen the bead if it was closed, then release it.\n    async fn handle_gate_failure(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n        report: &crate::validation::GateReport,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        // Find the first failing gate for telemetry.\n        let (failed_gate, reason) = report\n            .results\n            .iter()\n            .find(|(_, r)| !r.passed())\n            .map(|(name, r)| (name.clone(), r.failure_reason().unwrap_or(\"\").to_string()))\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| (\"unknown\".to_string(), \"unknown error\".to_string()));\n\n        tracing::warn!(\n            bead_id = %bead.id,\n            gate = %failed_gate,\n            reason = %reason,\n            \"validation gate failed — releasing bead\"\n        );\n\n        // Emit verification failure telemetry.\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::VerificationFailed {\n            bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n            command: failed_gate.clone(),\n            exit_code: None,\n            output: reason,\n        })?;\n\n        let mut events = Vec::new();\n\n        // If the agent already closed the bead, reopen it before releasing.\n        // Use timeout to prevent indefinite hang in HANDLING state.\n        match self.timeout_op(|| store.show(&bead.id), \"show\").await {\n            Ok(Some(current)) if current.status.is_done() => {\n                tracing::info!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"reopening bead closed by agent (verification failed)\"\n                );\n                match self.timeout_op(|| store.reopen(&bead.id), \"reopen\").await {\n                    Ok(_) => {}\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            bead_id = %bead.id,\n                            error = %e,\n                            \"failed to reopen bead — attempting release anyway\"\n                        );\n                        events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                            bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                            outcome: \"gate_failure\".to_string(),\n                            operation: \"reopen\".to_string(),\n                            error: e.to_string(),\n                        });\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            Ok(None) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"show() timed out during gate failure handling, skipping reopen\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"gate_failure\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"show\".to_string(),\n                    error: \"timeout after 30s\".to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"show() failed during gate failure handling\"\n                );\n            }\n            _ => {}\n        }\n\n        // Release the bead back to open with flush-before-release and sync recovery.\n        let mut release_events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n        events.append(&mut release_events);\n\n        // If release succeeded, increment failure count.\n        let release_succeeded = events\n            .iter()\n            .any(|e| matches!(e, EventKind::BeadReleased { .. }));\n        if release_succeeded {\n            if let Err(e) = self.increment_failure_count(store, bead).await {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to increment failure count after gate failure\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Add a label indicating verification failure.\n        if let Err(e) = tokio::time::timeout(\n            std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n            store.add_label(&bead.id, \"verification-failed\"),\n        )\n        .await\n        {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                error = %e,\n                \"failed to add verification-failed label\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok((BeadAction::Released, events))\n    }\n\n    /// Failure: release bead and increment failure count.\n    ///\n    /// Mitosis evaluation (for multi-task splitting) is handled externally by\n    /// the worker after outcome handling — see `MitosisEvaluator`.\n    ///\n    /// If br calls timeout or fail, logs the error and continues — does not\n    /// block the worker in HANDLING state indefinitely.\n    async fn handle_failure(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        tracing::warn!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"agent failure — releasing bead\");\n\n        let mut events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n\n        // If release succeeded, increment failure count.\n        // Check if the last event is BeadReleased (success) or BeadReleaseFailed (failure).\n        let release_succeeded = events\n            .iter()\n            .any(|e| matches!(e, EventKind::BeadReleased { .. }));\n        if release_succeeded {\n            if let Err(e) = self.increment_failure_count(store, bead).await {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to increment failure count after release\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Ensure we emit a reason event for telemetry.\n        if !events.iter().any(|e| {\n            matches!(\n                e,\n                EventKind::BeadReleased { .. } | EventKind::BeadReleaseFailed { .. }\n            )\n        }) {\n            events.push(EventKind::BeadReleased {\n                bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                reason: \"failure\".to_string(),\n            });\n        }\n\n        Ok((BeadAction::Released, events))\n    }\n\n    /// Timeout: release bead and add `deferred` label.\n    ///\n    /// If br calls timeout or fail, logs the error and continues — does not\n    /// block the worker in HANDLING state indefinitely.\n    async fn handle_timeout(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        tracing::warn!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"agent timed out — releasing bead as deferred\");\n\n        let mut events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n\n        // If release succeeded, increment failure count and add deferred label.\n        let release_succeeded = events\n            .iter()\n            .any(|e| matches!(e, EventKind::BeadReleased { .. }));\n        if release_succeeded {\n            // Increment failure count for auto-split tracking.\n            if let Err(e) = self.increment_failure_count(store, bead).await {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to increment failure count after timeout\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            if let Err(e) = tokio::time::timeout(\n                std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n                store.add_label(&bead.id, \"deferred\"),\n            )\n            .await\n            {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"add_label deferred timed out or failed after timeout release\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"timeout\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"add_label\".to_string(),\n                    error: e.to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok((BeadAction::Deferred, events))\n    }\n\n    /// Crash: release bead and create alert bead with diagnostic info.\n    async fn handle_crash(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n        signal_code: i32,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        tracing::error!(\n            bead_id = %bead.id,\n            signal_code,\n            agent = %self.config.agent.default,\n            \"agent crashed — releasing bead and creating alert\"\n        );\n\n        let events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n\n        // Create alert bead with diagnostic info (best-effort).\n        let signal_num = if signal_code > 128 {\n            signal_code - 128\n        } else {\n            signal_code\n        };\n        let timestamp = Utc::now().to_rfc3339();\n        let alert_title = format!(\"ALERT: Agent crash on bead {}\", bead.id);\n        let alert_body = format!(\n            \"## Agent Crash Report\\n\\\n             \\n\\\n             - **Bead ID**: {}\\n\\\n             - **Agent**: {}\\n\\\n             - **Exit code**: {} (signal {})\\n\\\n             - **Workspace**: {}\\n\\\n             - **Timestamp**: {}\\n\\\n             \\n\\\n             The agent process was killed. This bead has been released for retry.\",\n            bead.id,\n            self.config.agent.default,\n            signal_code,\n            signal_num,\n            bead.workspace.display(),\n            timestamp,\n        );\n\n        // Hook 4: propagate stitch labels from the crashed bead to the alert.\n        let signal_label = format!(\"signal-{}\", signal_num);\n        let mut alert_labels: Vec<String> = vec![\"alert\".into(), \"crash\".into(), signal_label];\n        alert_labels.extend(crate::types::extract_stitch_labels(&bead.labels));\n        let alert_label_refs: Vec<&str> = alert_labels.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();\n        match tokio::time::timeout(\n            std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n            store.create_bead(&alert_title, &alert_body, &alert_label_refs),\n        )\n        .await\n        {\n            Ok(Ok(alert_id)) => {\n                tracing::info!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    %alert_id,\n                    \"crash alert bead created\"\n                );\n            }\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to create crash alert bead\"\n                );\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"create_bead timed out after 30s during crash handling\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok((BeadAction::Alerted, events))\n    }\n\n    /// AgentNotFound: release bead, emit error. No retry — this is a config issue.\n    async fn handle_agent_not_found(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        tracing::error!(\n            bead_id = %bead.id,\n            agent = %self.config.agent.default,\n            \"agent binary not found — releasing bead (config issue, no retry)\"\n        );\n\n        let events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n        Ok((BeadAction::Released, events))\n    }\n\n    /// Interrupted: release bead for graceful shutdown.\n    async fn handle_interrupted(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        tracing::info!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"agent interrupted — releasing bead for clean shutdown\");\n\n        let events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n        Ok((BeadAction::Released, events))\n    }\n\n    /// Increment the failure count label on a bead.\n    ///\n    /// Labels follow the pattern `failure-count:N`. If `failure-count:2` exists,\n    /// the old label is removed and `failure-count:3` is added.\n    ///\n    /// All `br` calls are wrapped in timeouts to prevent indefinite hang in\n    /// HANDLING state. Failures are non-fatal — we log and continue.\n    async fn increment_failure_count(&self, store: &dyn BeadStore, bead: &Bead) -> Result<()> {\n        // Read labels with timeout.\n        let labels =\n            match tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30), store.labels(&bead.id))\n                .await\n            {\n                Ok(Ok(l)) => l,\n                Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"could not read labels to increment failure count\"\n                    );\n                    return Ok(());\n                }\n                Err(_) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        \"labels() timed out after 30s, skipping failure count increment\"\n                    );\n                    return Ok(());\n                }\n            };\n\n        let current_count = labels\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|l| l.strip_prefix(\"failure-count:\"))\n            .filter_map(|n| n.parse::<u32>().ok())\n            .max()\n            .unwrap_or(0);\n\n        let new_count = current_count + 1;\n        let new_label = format!(\"failure-count:{}\", new_count);\n\n        // Remove old failure-count labels before adding the new one.\n        // Each remove_label call is wrapped in a timeout.\n        for label in &labels {\n            if label.starts_with(\"failure-count:\") {\n                match tokio::time::timeout(\n                    std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n                    store.remove_label(&bead.id, label),\n                )\n                .await\n                {\n                    Ok(Ok(())) => {}\n                    Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            bead_id = %bead.id,\n                            label,\n                            error = %e,\n                            \"failed to remove old failure-count label\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            bead_id = %bead.id,\n                            label,\n                            \"remove_label timed out after 30s\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Add the new label with timeout.\n        match tokio::time::timeout(\n            std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n            store.add_label(&bead.id, &new_label),\n        )\n        .await\n        {\n            Ok(Ok(())) => {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    count = new_count,\n                    \"failure count incremented\"\n                );\n            }\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to add failure-count label\"\n                );\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"add_label timed out after 30s\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Reset the failure count label on a bead by removing all `failure-count:N` labels.\n    ///\n    /// Called on success to clear the failure counter so the bead starts fresh\n    /// on the next cycle.\n    ///\n    /// All `br` calls are wrapped in timeouts to prevent indefinite hang in\n    /// HANDLING state. Failures are non-fatal — we log and continue.\n    async fn reset_failure_count(&self, store: &dyn BeadStore, bead: &Bead) -> Result<()> {\n        // Read labels with timeout.\n        let labels =\n            match tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30), store.labels(&bead.id))\n                .await\n            {\n                Ok(Ok(l)) => l,\n                Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"could not read labels to reset failure count\"\n                    );\n                    return Ok(());\n                }\n                Err(_) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        \"labels() timed out after 30s, skipping failure count reset\"\n                    );\n                    return Ok(());\n                }\n            };\n\n        // Remove all failure-count labels.\n        let mut removed_count = 0;\n        for label in &labels {\n            if label.starts_with(\"failure-count:\") {\n                match tokio::time::timeout(\n                    std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n                    store.remove_label(&bead.id, label),\n                )\n                .await\n                {\n                    Ok(Ok(())) => {\n                        removed_count += 1;\n                    }\n                    Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            bead_id = %bead.id,\n                            label,\n                            error = %e,\n                            \"failed to remove failure-count label\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            bead_id = %bead.id,\n                            label,\n                            \"remove_label timed out after 30s\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        if removed_count > 0 {\n            tracing::debug!(\n                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                removed_count,\n                \"failure count reset\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// \"Interrupted\"),\n            Outcome::Crash(code) => write!(f, \"Crash({})\", code),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Callers should treat timeout and error as non-fatal — log\n    /// and continue rather than blocking the worker in HANDLING state.\n    async fn timeout_op<T, F, Fut>(\n        &self,\n        op: F,\n        operation_name: &str,\n    ) -> Result<Option<T>, anyhow::Error>\n    where\n        F: FnOnce() -> Fut,\n        Fut: std::future::Future<Output = Result<T, anyhow::Error>>,\n    {\n        match tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30), op()).await {\n            Ok(Ok(result)) => Ok(Some(result)),\n            Ok(Err(e)) => Err(e),\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::error!(\n                    operation = operation_name,\n                    \"bead store operation timed out after 30s\"\n                );\n                Ok(None)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Release a bead with sync conflict recovery and graceful failure handling.\n    ///\n    /// Flow:\n    /// 1. 1: Flush local writes to JSONL before attempting release.\n        // Emit heartbeat before br call to track where hang occurs.\n        let _ = self.timeout_op(|| store.flush(), \"flush\").await {\n            Ok(Some(())) => {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"flushed local changes to JSONL before release\"\n                );\n                // Emit heartbeat after successful flush.\n                let _ = self.telemetry.emit_try_lock(EventKind::HeartbeatEmitted {\n                    bead_id: Some(bead.id.clone()),\n                    state: \"HANDLING_FLUSH_DONE\".to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n            Ok(None) => {\n events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"release\".to_string(),\n                    operation:                 state: \"HANDLING_RELEASE_DONE\".to_string(),\n                });\n                events.push(EventKind::BeadReleased {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n   bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"br release failed after SYNC_CONFLICT recovery — \\\n                         worker will continue (bead may events.push(EventKind::BeadReleaseFailed {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    reason: \"timeout after 30s\".to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(events)\n    }\n\n    /// Handle a process output for the given bead.\n    ///\n    /// Uses `classify()` to determine the outcome, then dispatches to the\n    /// per-outcome handler. This prevents the handler from making further br calls\n    /// after a timeout has occurred.\n    pub async fn handle_with_cancellation(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: early\"\n            );\n            // Return a default HandlerResult to allow the worker to recover.\n            return Ok(HandlerResult {\n                outcome: classify(output.exit_code, indefinite hangs.\n        // This is a safety net in case the internal br call timeouts don't work.\n        let bead_id = bead.id.clone();\n        let telemetry = self.telemetry.clone();\n\n        match tokio::time::timeout(\n            std::time::Duration::from_secs(50),\n            self.handle(store, bead, output, was_interrupted),\n        )\n        .await\n        {\n            Ok(Ok(result)) => Ok(result),\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                // Handler returned an error.\n                tracing::error!(\n                    bead_id = %bead_id,\n             // Emit a timeout event for observability.\n                let _ = telemetry.emit(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                    outcome: classify(output.exit_code, was_interrupted)\n                        .as_str()\n                        .to_string(),\n                    operation: \"handle\".to_string(),\n
